UNITY-GLOBHEALTH-2025.name: Global Health Unity
UNITY-GLOBHEALTH-2025.description: International collaborative network for global health initiatives

WHO-001.name: WHO
WHO-001.description: International public health organization coordinating health initiatives and emergency responses worldwide
WHO-001.duty: Set global health standards, coordinate pandemic responses, and provide technical support to countries
WHO-001.fundingSource: Member state contributions (20%), voluntary donations from governments and foundations (80%)

UNICEF-001.name: UNICEF
UNICEF-001.description: Global humanitarian organization focused on children's rights, survival, development and protection
UNICEF-001.duty: Provide emergency relief, education, healthcare and nutrition programs for children in crisis zones
UNICEF-001.fundingSource: Voluntary contributions from governments (70%), private sector partnerships (20%), individual donations (10%)

REDC-001.name: Red Cross
REDC-001.fullName: International Committee of the Red Cross
REDC-001.description: Humanitarian organization providing emergency assistance, disaster relief and education in communities worldwide
REDC-001.duty: Protect victims of armed conflict, provide disaster response, and promote humanitarian law compliance
REDC-001.fundingSource: Government donations (65%), public fundraising (25%), corporate partnerships (10%)

MSF-001.name: MSF
MSF-001.description: International medical humanitarian organization delivering emergency aid to people affected by conflict, epidemics, and disasters
MSF-001.duty: Provide emergency medical care in conflict zones, treat epidemic diseases, and operate mobile clinics

CDC-001.name: CDC
CDC-001.fullName: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
CDC-001.description: National public health institute leading science-based disease prevention and health promotion initiatives
CDC-001.duty: Monitor and investigate disease outbreaks, develop prevention strategies, and provide health guidelines
CDC-001.fundingSource: Federal government appropriations (85%), user fees and reimbursements (15%)

GAVI-001.name: GAVI
GAVI-001.fullName: Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization
GAVI-001.description: Public-private partnership increasing access to immunization in poor countries through vaccine procurement and health system strengthening
GAVI-001.duty: Accelerate vaccine access, strengthen immunization systems, and negotiate affordable vaccine prices
GAVI-001.fundingSource: Donor governments (60%), Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (20%), private sector (10%), innovative financing (10%)

WBANK-001.name: World Bank
WBANK-001.description: International financial institution providing loans and grants to governments for capital projects and economic development
WBANK-001.duty: Finance infrastructure projects, reduce poverty through economic development, and provide technical expertise
WBANK-001.fundingSource: Bond issuances in capital markets (70%), member country subscriptions (20%), loan repayments (10%)

GATES-001.name: Gates Foundation
GATES-001.description: Private philanthropic organization focused on global health, poverty alleviation, and expanding educational opportunities
GATES-001.duty: Fund health innovation, support vaccine development, improve agricultural productivity in developing countries
GATES-001.fundingSource: Endowment from Bill and Melinda Gates (95%), Warren Buffett contributions (5%)

HARV-001.name: Harvard
HARV-001.description: Private Ivy League research university conducting advanced medical and public health research
HARV-001.duty: Conduct health policy research, train global health professionals, and develop innovative treatment protocols
HARV-001.fundingSource: Endowment returns (35%), research grants (30%), tuition and fees (20%), donations (15%)

OXFD-001.name: Oxford
OXFD-001.description: Collegiate research university leading vaccine development and global health research initiatives
OXFD-001.duty: Develop vaccines and treatments, conduct epidemiological research, and train healthcare leaders
OXFD-001.fundingSource: Research grants (40%), endowment and investments (25%), tuition fees (20%), government funding (15%)

MEET-002.outcome: Developed unified early warning system for disease outbreaks across three continents

MEET-008.purpose: Establish secure framework for sharing health data across international organizations

MEET-009.title: Disaster Relief Coordination
MEET-009.purpose: Coordinate disaster relief operations and resource allocation for recent flooding events

MEET-011.title: Education in Health Workshop
MEET-011.purpose: Develop educational programs to improve health literacy in underserved communities
MEET-011.outcome: Launched 10 pilot health education programs in partnership with local schools

MEET-012.title: Funding Opportunities Discussion
MEET-012.purpose: Explore funding opportunities and investment strategies for health initiatives
MEET-012.outcome: Secured $200M in funding commitments for vaccine research and distribution programs

MEET-013.title: Research Collaboration Meeting
MEET-013.purpose: Establish research partnerships for developing new treatment protocols and medications
MEET-013.outcome: Initiated 5 joint research projects on infectious disease treatment innovations

MEET-014.title: Global Health Financing
MEET-014.purpose: Discuss sustainable financing models for long-term global health programs
MEET-014.outcome: Approved innovative financing mechanism generating $500M over 5 years

MEET-015.title: Emergency Preparedness Training
MEET-015.purpose: Conduct emergency preparedness drills and update response protocols for health workers
MEET-015.outcome: Trained 500 healthcare workers and updated emergency response guidelines
